mandatory_contract_terms: The child identity remains cav2.define.system-runtime.v1 with ontology type system-runtime, branch system, private visibility, and authority_effect none.
The child remains separately owned by the CyberAlchemy v2 Define runtime owner and keeps its own validator and append-only receipt boundary.
The runtime owner may maintain the candidate system model and later decide one exact implementation contract, but may not change Define product meaning or public Invoke ownership.
Candidate status, source currentness, schema validation, Project membership, and child-package topology must not become adoption, implementation, or authority by implication.
extension_scope: candidate system-runtime components, interfaces, workflows, policies, state, relations, views, and evidence under cav2.define.system-runtime.v1
runtime-local realization details that preserve the parent Define capability meaning and authority boundaries
future exact implementation-contract candidates routed separately to the Define runtime owner
forbidden_redefinitions: changing parent Define product meaning through a system-ontology record
changing canonical definitions or public Invoke ownership through runtime ownership
treating child-package topology as an admitted CAV2-D16 model-instance relation
treating candidate identity, conformance, validation, or receipts as adoption or implementation authority
contracts.challenge_route: Challenge parent Define product meaning through the CyberAlchemy v2 product owner; challenge child runtime-model meaning and any adoption or implementation-contract claim through the Define runtime owner; route canonical definitions and public migration separately.

claim_ceiling: Exact candidate-state inheritance proposal only; no semantic release version, adoption decision, conformance, D64 binding, runtime acceptance, implementation, publication, or external effect.
